subject: Observability hooks & SDK integration - post-call recap + next steps
content:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Observability hooks & SDK integration - post-call recap + next steps

Hi Alex — great call today, thanks for walking through your integration surface and the routing constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Use case: low-latency customer-facing inference for fraud detection scoring + async batch reranking for nightly re-score.
- Integration: you’ll use our Node SDK or HTTP API through your Kong edge router.
- Auth: API keys for service-to-service; short-lived tokens for finer security controls.
- Routing: route by model capability + latency SLO (edge -> dedicated -> hosted fallback).
- Structured output & tool-calling: JSON-schema validated function calls supported in the SDK.
- Embeddings/reranker: embeddings for similarity search, reranker for pairwise scoring; both available via API endpoints.
- Observability: attach Redwood trace/request headers and our latency breakdown header to logs so your dashboards can show token-level breakdowns.

Immediate asks/action items:
1) Tech sample snippets: Dylan will send Node/Python SDK snippets + example curl commands (auth, headers, routing).
2) SDK/auth: we’ll provide a short-lived token workflow and example Kong config for forwarding headers (see sample header names below).
3) Cost/SLO sizing: Elliot to follow up with a rough per-request unit-cost for embeddings vs reranker and expected latency at p50/p95 for your traffic profile.
4) Dashboarding/Events: we shared a sample log line and dashboard link (attached + HubSpot).
5) Schedule follow-up: please book a 30-min technical sync on our Calendly if you want to deep-dive.

Suggested observability hooks (examples) - please share with your infra team:
- Request/trace headers:
  - Redwood-Request-Id: unique request id visible end-to-end
  - X-Redwood-Trace-Id: trace id useful for correlating with APM
  - X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: kernel_ms=12;kv_cache_ms=2;network_ms=8;total_ms=22
  - X-Redwood-Model: gpt-redwood-1-large

- Log fields (JSON) to emit on every inference response:
  - trace_id, request_id, model, route, latency_ms, token_count, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, kernel_ms, total_ms

- Example log line (single-line JSON):
  {"timestamp":"2026-08-10T15:11:59Z", "trace_id":"abcd-1234", "request_id":"r-98765", "model":"gpt-redwood-1-large", "route":"dedicated-us-west-2", "latency_ms":22, "kernel_ms":12, "kv_cache_ms":2, "network_ms":8, "token_count":48} 

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (one-page checklist), sample-logs.txt (example log lines).

Next steps from our side: Dylan will send the SDK snippets and a short Kong config sample by EOD. Elliot will share a cost/SLO estimate by Wednesday.

Thanks — feel free to reply with any missing pieces or book a sync: https://calendly.com/marissa-co/30min

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Alex — Dylan from the integration team here. Quick answers and snippets inline.

Auth:
- We support long-lived API keys and short-lived bearer tokens (JWTs) that can be minted via our token exchange endpoint. Recommended pattern: service-to-service uses a signed client credential to request a short-lived token (~15m) and then use that for calls.

Kong config (example):
- Ensure you preserve headers: Redwood-Request-Id, X-Redwood-Trace-Id, X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown. Example snippet for Kong plugin config to preserve headers when proxying to origin. (I’ll attach a file with a full example.)

Sample curl (text generation):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \ \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>" \ 
  -H "Redwood-Request-Id: r-98765" \ 
  -H "X-Redwood-Trace-Id: abcd-1234" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1-large","input":"Explain the origin of transaction anomaly...","max_tokens":64}'

Node SDK (example):
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ token: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-redwood-1-large', input: '...' , requestId: 'r-98765', traceId: 'abcd-1234' });

Embeddings/reranker notes:
- Embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings (512-d floats by default; we can configure to 384/1024)
- Reranker: POST /v1/rerank (pairwise/ranking mode) — reranker runs cheaper per inference than full-gen for short pairwise signals but depends on list size.

Observability headers and recommended usage:
- Redwood-Request-Id: unique per customer request (correlates across services)
- X-Redwood-Trace-Id: tie to your APM traces
- X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: semicolon-delimited key=ms to keep logs parseable

Example X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown value:
  kernel_ms=12;kv_cache_ms=2;batch_overhead_ms=3;network_ms=8;total_ms=25

Log JSON example for ingestion into your ELK/Datadog: 
{"timestamp":"2026-08-10T17:04:59Z","trace_id":"abcd-1234","request_id":"r-98765","model":"gpt-redwood-1-large","route":"dedicated-us-west-2","kernel_ms":12,"kv_cache_ms":2,"network_ms":8,"total_ms":22,"token_count":48,"batch_size":1}

I’ve attached the Kong example + SDK snippets (sdk-snippets.zip). Happy to hop on a call to walk through the Kong plugin if useful.

Dylan
